prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished desktop website design comp, 1536x1024 landscape: a real web layout, edge to edge, no device frame, no browser chrome.

The attached reference images are screenshots of the SAME website's already-built pages (the homepage and the Walkthrough page). Carry over exactly: the header (script wordmark "Birdcar" at left; nav "How I work", "Selected work", "Writing" and a canary-yellow pill "Book a free Walkthrough →"), the pale daylight ground #edf3f0, near-black ink #0b141a, the heavy tight grotesk (Mona Sans) for all text, white cards with soft offset shadows, white pill tags, canary yellow #f7c848 only on actions and on small glowing packet cubes that travel dotted routes, teal #5fb8bf only for a resolved or "working" state, and the premium matte isometric miniature render style (soft studio daylight, fine architectural-model detail, pale wood, matte stone, teal-cyan floor tiles, tiny realistic figures, a small canary). Do NOT copy any reference's content: no homepage headline, no desk from the Walkthrough, no logo strip.

This page is "Selected work": a single work story about Craft & Communicate, a marketing agency. The only facts: the agency's client reporting involved finding performance numbers by hand; Nick (Birdcar) built a client-facing reporting platform with client management and live-updating data; the platform is now an offering the agency can sell to its customers. Any screen shown inside a miniature is an illustration: abstract chart lines and bars only, no numbers, no percentages, no metrics, no logos, no readable text on screens. The visitor's job: believe Nick builds real, useful systems, then book a Walkthrough.

STRUCTURE, in reading order (before and after: one miniature of the agency, switched between two states):
1. Header, about 80px, as the reference.
2. First viewport. LEFT (x 80 to 620): headline about 76px, two lines: "Craft & Communicate". A lead at about 22px: "A reporting platform that's part of the agency's service, not just the work behind it." Then a small muted line: "Illustrated. Not a product screenshot or measured results."
RIGHT (x 660 to 1480, y 110 to 960): the dominant object, a premium matte isometric floating-slab diorama of a small marketing agency office cut away like an architectural model: a few desks with tiny figures, a meeting table, and a front area where the agency's clients arrive. It is shown in its AFTER state: at the center a clean reporting console module with abstract teal chart lines, live teal lanes running from it to two small client desks at the edge of the slab where tiny client figures look at the same abstract charts; a few glowing packet cubes travel those lanes. White pill tags name the parts: "Performance data", "Client management", "Part of the agency's service". Above the diorama, top left, a white segmented pill control with two options, "Before" and "After", with "After" selected in solid ink with white text.
3. Bottom band (y 960 to 1024) on white: the top of the next section heading, "Getting the numbers was part of the work."

ART DIRECTION: one dominant move, the diorama in its after state; everything else holds still. Premium, adult, precise. Not cute. No purple, no gradient orbs, no robots, no AI imagery, no stock photos, no numbers or results, no testimonials, no client logos. Preserve all quoted words exactly. Treat it as a finished, shippable website.
